metaDesc: Our ranking of 11 real, open mountain-view cafes in Khao Kho, Thailand — from Pino Latte behind Wat Pha Sorn Kaew and B.N. Farm to Route 12 and flower-field cafes, with prices, areas, and the best time to catch the sea of fog.

ogTitle: 11 Mountain-View Cafes in Khao Kho — Coffee Above the Fog
ogDesc: Real, open Khao Kho cafes with mountain views, sea of fog, tea farms, and flower fields — plus prices and areas.
h1:
Khao Kho Cafes
Coffee Above the Sea of Fog
intro: Khao Kho sits at around 800–1,000 metres, so the air stays cool most of the year. From late rainy season into winter (October–February) a sea of fog rolls across the valley each morning. Cafes up here don't really sell coffee — they sell the view. We picked 11 that are genuinely open, lined up by the kind of scenery they offer, from the famous spot behind Wat Pha Sorn Kaew to tea-farm and flower-field cafes and roadside stops along Highway 12. We'll tell you straight which ones win on the view and which actually do good coffee.

blocks.html: Before we run through them one by one, one honest thing up front: at most Khao Kho cafes the view comes before the coffee. A lot of the spots with the best views only score so-so on taste in reviews, while the cafes that take their coffee seriously usually have a smaller view. So we ranked them by weighing the view, the atmosphere, and the price together, which lets you pick based on what you're actually after.

blocks.text: Ranking the 11 Best Mountain-View Cafes in Khao Kho

items.name: Pino Latte Resort & Cafe
items.blurb: The most famous cafe in Khao Kho. You sit at a long bar running along the balcony with an open mountain view of more than 180 degrees and nothing in the way. On winter mornings you'll see the sea of fog drifting over the valley, with Pha Sorn Kaew pagoda in the distance. To be honest the coffee is middling — people come for the view and the photo angles. It gets packed on weekends, so arrive before 9am to grab a spot along the balcony.
items.meta: Khaem Son (behind Wat Pha Sorn Kaew) · Open 08:00–19:00 (Mon–Fri from 10:30)

items.name: B.N. Farm — The Front
items.blurb: An old farm dating back to 1969. Across from the farm entrance, the cafe zone called The Front has a wide grassy lawn on the hillside, a field of cosmos flowers, and seasonal strawberry rows. It's a good place to bring the family for a wander and some photos before sitting down for coffee, and prices are friendlier than the hilltop view cafes.

items.name: The Dreamer Khaokho
items.blurb: A small, minimalist cafe in a curvy building that looks like a house out of a storybook, near Wat Pha Sorn Kaew. There's a window-frame spot that opens onto the mountains as a backdrop. It's a pretty cafe for photos that hasn't been overrun the way the bigger places have.
items.meta: Near Wat Pha Sorn Kaew · Open 10:00–17:00

items.name: Route 12 Coffee
items.blurb: A coffee stop along Highway 12 (Phitsanulok–Lom Sak) around km 95, with a warm, retro design. It's a popular pit stop on the drive up to Khao Kho and has the cheapest coffee on this list, perfect for resting your legs before pushing on. No sea-of-fog view, but the place is charming and easy to park.

items.name: Loyrhom Khaokho
items.blurb: The name means "floating on the wind," which fits its hillside spot that takes in the full sweep of the mountains. It stays open until 9pm, so you can sit anywhere from the morning sea of fog through the sunset and evening lights. Great for groups of friends who want to settle in and chill for a while.

items.name: 180 Cafe Khaokho
items.blurb: The name says it all — a wide 180-degree view, with a wooden deck that juts out over the valley. It's another spot where you can clearly see the sea of fog on winter mornings, and it opens at seven, right in time for the fog window.

items.name: Hydrangea Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe set in a cool-climate flower garden on a hillside. The draw is the hydrangeas and marguerite daisies that bloom at certain times of year, so it suits anyone into flower photography. The atmosphere is fresh and breezy — just check before you go whether anything is in bloom.
items.price: Coffee ฿60–80 · Garden entry fee at certain times

items.name: Phukaew Peak Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe on high ground with a panoramic view of layered mountain ridges. On clear days it's a great angle for seeing the Khao Kho ranges, ideal if you like an open view with nothing blocking it.

items.name: Cedar Pine Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe tucked into a pine grove that feels cool and shaded, like sitting in the forest. It's about calm rather than a sweeping valley view, so it's good if you want to escape the crowds and sit quietly over a single cup.

items.name: Bankhao Cafe
items.blurb: A well-placed mountain-view cafe that stays open until 7pm. The design is clean and easy-going — nothing flashy, but a comfortable place to sit and take in the view. A solid backup when the famous spots are crammed.

items.name: The Piney Bistro Cafe
items.blurb: Located behind Wat Pha Sorn Kaew, with a view out over pine trees and mountains. It pairs naturally with a temple visit, and it's a bistro with proper main dishes, not just coffee — good for lunch after touring the temple.
items.meta: Behind Wat Pha Sorn Kaew · Open 09:00–18:00

blocks.title: What time do you need to arrive to see the sea of fog?
blocks.html: The Khao Kho sea of fog shows up from late rainy season into early winter (October–February), and it's thickest around 05:30–07:00. Once the sun is up it gradually thins out within an hour or two. If you're coming specifically for the fog, pick a cafe that opens at seven (like 180 Cafe or Route 12), or head to a viewpoint first and stop by a cafe later in the morning.

blocks.text: How to Pick the Right Cafe for Your Trip

items: For the view + photos — Pino Latte, 180 Cafe, and Phukaew Peak have the most open, sweeping views, but they fill up on weekends, so go early for a good spot.
With family/kids — B.N. Farm's The Front has a grassy lawn, flower fields, and strawberry rows to wander through, so nobody has to sit still all day.
Coffee lovers on a budget — Route 12 is the cheapest and makes a good pit stop before heading up the mountain; B.N. Farm is also easy on the wallet.
Want somewhere quiet — Cedar Pine in the pine grove, or The Dreamer, which hasn't been overrun yet — both good for dodging the crowds.
Coming in the evening/at night — Loyrhom stays open until 9pm, so you can watch the sunset and the evening lights.

blocks.text: Popular Stops on the Way Up to Khao Kho

blocks.html: The most popular route up to Khao Kho is to come in on Highway 12 (Phitsanulok–Lom Sak) and then turn onto Route 2196 to climb the mountain. Along the way there are a few stops where people like to pull over to rest and take photos before reaching the hilltop cafes.

items.name: Route 12 Coffee (km 95)
items.blurb: A rest stop before the turn up the mountain. Cheap coffee, easy parking, perfect for stretching your legs after a long drive.

items.name: Wat Pha Sorn Kaew
items.blurb: A hilltop temple covered in colourful mosaic tiles with lovely mountain views — a landmark that goes hand in hand with the cafes around Khaem Son.

items.name: B.N. Farm / The Front
items.blurb: Flower fields, strawberry rows, and a cafe all in one place — stop by before or after heading up to the summit.

blocks.title: What to know before you go
blocks.html: Mobile signal is weak in spots up on Khao Kho, so screenshot your map ahead of time · many cafes are cash or QR-scan only, so bring both · in winter (Nov–Jan) it gets very busy and rooms book out fast, so reserve ahead · some stretches of the mountain road are steep and winding, so make sure your brakes are good and drive during the day for more safety.

faq.q: Which Khao Kho cafe has the best view?
faq.a: If you're judging by the width of the view, Pino Latte and 180 Cafe both open onto more than 180 degrees of mountains with nothing in the way, and you'll clearly see the sea of fog on winter mornings. But both get very busy on weekends, so arrive before 9am to claim a spot along the balcony.

faq.q: When should I go to Khao Kho to see the sea of fog?
faq.a: The sea of fog comes from late rainy season into early winter, roughly October to February, and it's thickest in the early morning around 05:30–07:00. Once the sun is up it thins out within 1–2 hours, so get up early and pick a cafe that opens at seven.

faq.q: How much does coffee cost at Khao Kho cafes?
faq.a: At most hilltop view cafes, coffee runs about ฿60–110 a cup. Famous spots like Pino Latte are a bit higher at around ฿95–110, while roadside places like Route 12 are cheaper at around ฿35–45.

faq.q: Do I need my own car to visit the Khao Kho cafes?
faq.a: Driving yourself is by far the easiest, since the cafes are spread out across the hills and along Route 2196 with a fair distance between them, and there's no public transport that goes right to the door. If you don't have a car, you can rent one or hire a local driver to take you around for the day.

faq.q: Which Khao Kho cafe is best for kids and families?
faq.a: B.N. Farm's The Front is the best fit, with a wide grassy lawn, a field of cosmos flowers, and seasonal strawberry rows to wander through, so kids don't have to sit still — and it's friendlier on the wallet than the hilltop view cafes.
